subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The profit function P(x) of a company selling x items per day is given by P(x) = (150 − x)x − 1600. Find the number of items that the company should sell to get the maximum profit. Also find the maximum profit.

mark_split.label: Expand the profit function and differentiate

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you do to the bracket before differentiating, and say the two things the question asks you to report.

steps.label: Expand the profit function and differentiate
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply the bracket out first — the expanded form shows at once that P is a downward parabola in x. The constant −1600 differentiates to zero.
lines: P(x) = (150 − x)x − 1600,  where x is the number of items sold per day.
The coefficient of x² is negative, so the graph of P is a downward parabola.

accept: expand the bracket to get one fifty x minus x squared minus sixteen hundred
the derivative is one fifty minus two x

differentiate the profit function first

steps.why: Expanding turns a product into a plain quadratic, so one differentiation gives a linear equation. The fixed cost 1600 does not change with x, so it disappears on differentiating.
common_mistakes: Differentiating the product (150 − x)x as (−1)(1) and losing both terms.
Carrying the −1600 through into the derivative.
steps.memory_tip: A constant cost never changes WHERE the profit is greatest, only how large that greatest profit is. It vanishes in the derivative and returns only in the final substitution.

steps.label: Solve P′(x) = 0
steps.margin_note: Second mark. This answers the first half of the question — the number of items. x = 75 is a whole number, which suits a count of items.
lines: For the stationary point, put P′(x) = 0.
x = 75 is a whole number, which is what a count of items must be.

the company should sell seventy five items
derivative zero pettina x seventy five vasthundi
two x is one fifty so x is seventy five
the stationary point is at seventy five items

steps.why: The profit stops rising and starts falling where its rate of change is zero, so P′ = 0 locates the number of items being asked for.
common_mistakes: Reading 150 as the answer because it appears in the question.
steps.memory_tip: For P = ax² + bx + c the stationary point is at x = −b/(2a). Here that is 150/2 = 75, which is a quick check on the algebra.

steps.label: Confirm the maximum
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Write P″ and state its sign. A stationary point is not a maximum until the test says so, even when the shape of the graph makes it obvious.
lines: A negative second derivative means the stationary point is a maximum.
So the profit is greatest when x = 75 items are sold per day.

recall.must_convey: That P″(x) = −2 < 0, which proves x = 75 gives the maximum profit.

negative so it is a maximum

confirm it is a maximum and not a minimum

steps.why: Setting the derivative to zero alone cannot tell a greatest profit from a smallest one. The sign of P″ is the proof, and it carries its own mark even for a quadratic.
common_mistakes: Skipping the test because the answer looks obvious from the shape.
Writing P″ = 2 and then claiming a maximum, which contradicts itself.
steps.memory_tip: For any quadratic the second derivative is the constant 2a. Here a = −1, so P″ = −2 and the sign is settled in one line.

steps.label: Find the maximum profit
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The question asks for TWO things, so the profit value must be computed as well. Substitute into the ORIGINAL P(x), not into the derivative.

lines.text: ∴ the company should sell 75 items per day, and the maximum profit is 4025

recall.must_convey: That P(75) = 5625 − 1600 = 4025, so the maximum profit is 4025 at 75 items.

steps.why: The question asks for the number of items and for the profit, so an answer that stops at x = 75 is only half done. Substituting into the original P(x) brings the fixed cost back in.
common_mistakes: Stopping at x = 75 and never computing the profit.
Substituting into P′(x), which gives 0 and not the profit.
Forgetting to subtract the 1600 and writing 5625.
steps.memory_tip: Substitute into the ORIGINAL function for the value, never into the derivative — the derivative is zero there, which is how the point was found.
